messages.author: 47cf8f9db29d976d
messages.subject: output of regionCounts function
parts:
Hi,
I used output<-regionCounts(methObj,regions) to figure out methylation information of the regions of interest. However, the output object had shorter length than that of regions. This is a bit strange because it's expected to return an object with the same length as the input one. I would like to ask why this happened and how regionCounts calculates the output?
Thanks in advance.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: output of regionCounts function
parts:
if there are regions with no read coverage in your "regions" object, they won't be outputted in the resulting "output" object.

Best,
Altuna

parts:
Hi,
Thanks for your reply.
I've checked the data and found that the number of regions was reduced enormously after regionCounts (from more than 30000 to 16000, meaning that methylation counts for about half of them could not be called). This is very strange. To verify, I randomly took a region absent in the "output" object and checked its methylation status on genome browser, and in fact it had many methylated bases. Could you please check how the regionCounts works to see why this happened?
Many thanks.

messages.subject: Re: output of regionCounts function
parts:
One more thing to try before trying to get the reproducible example.
Try setting the strand of your regions of interest to "*".

#my.regions is a GRanges object
strand(my.regions) <- "*"

then try regionCounts with destranded regions, I suspect this may
happen because regionCounts is trying to match the strands of CpGs
with the strands of the GRanges object.

If that doesn't help, please send me the reproducible example.

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: output of regionCounts function
parts:
Yes, I noticed strand.aware is currently doing opposite of what is
supposed to do. Thanks for pointing this out, it should be fixed in
the next version. For now, setting the strand manually to "*" is the
best way to avoid the confusion created by the strand.aware parameter.

Best,
Altuna
